fatal_errors: No prior evidence is supplied for the proposed short-range-order mechanism.

Composition is changed without independently controlling short-range order, so any property correlation cannot distinguish SRO effects from lattice distortion, elastic-modulus changes, stacking-fault energy, or conventional solid-solution strengthening.
The investigation omits the temperature-dependent single-crystal CRSS, strain-rate-jump, serrated-flow, TEM, and lattice-distortion measurements central to the target mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad question of why Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni subsets can have different mechanical properties and proposes a testable atomic-scale mediator. Its quinary baseline, single-phase-FCC boundary, and explicit falsification rule are useful. However, it is not a close reconstruction of the target study. The target concerns [1̄23]-oriented single-crystal compression over 9–1373 K and identifies three linked effects: MSAD-controlled solid-solution strength, phonon-drag-controlled inertial dulling below roughly 60–77 K, and Mn/Fe-associated Cottrell-type Portevin–Le Chatelier pinning at high temperature. The generated answer instead invokes SRO, gives only nondirectional predictions for unspecified subsets, and focuses on tensile strength, hardening, and ductility under unspecified conditions. Its experiment could detect an SRO–property association, but changing composition simultaneously changes many other strengthening variables, so it would not establish causality without independently varying SRO at fixed composition or using multivariate mechanistic measurements. The complete absence of supporting evidence is especially consequential because the prompt explicitly requests prior evidence. Thus, this is a scientifically plausible but weakly supported alternative rather than a reconstruction of the hidden target.
